mutants.why: This restores the closeout regression caught by the first full gate: an S.A.K.-formatted >1.35 TiB container whose multi-block IP ring moved during chunk-adding grow does not match the canonical slot computed from its new size. Routing it into the one-block foreign path blocks the certified shrink. apfsWriter_growsMultiChunkSourceContainer builds that exact 11000->11500->10900-chunk chain and requires commit.ok; the mutant fails with the multi-block foreign-bitmap blocker.

A genuine Apple commit can place its newly allocated CIB at an address that resembles one of S.A.K.'s generated slots. Removing authenticated formatted_by provenance then forgets the media is foreign and re-enters the generated allocator. apfsWriter_foreignMultiCibRotationExcludesEveryLiveBitmap reconstructs the genuine post-insert 135-chunk/2-CIB state; the mutant misclassifies it and the exact live far-bitmap assertions fail.

The IP CIB/bitmap ring has live, previous, and spare slots, so a block ages into reuse after two later checkpoints. Reusing the main-data queue's four-checkpoint window leaves the genuine 256 MiB internal pool with no reusable CIB/bitmap pair. apfsWriter_foreignMultiChunkCowInsertRoundTrips requires the real Apple insert to succeed; the mutant returns the exact no-reusable-block refusal.

Keeping only chunk 0's bitmap omits live allocation bitmaps owned by later CIB entries; the allocator can then overwrite one as if it were a free IP block. apfsWriter_foreignMultiCibRotationExcludesEveryLiveBitmap pins genuine chunk-3 bitmap block 10900 as authenticated live metadata and unavailable. The mutant makes foreignIpBlockIsLiveMetadataForTesting return false.

The foreign finalize must publish the rebuilt IP free queue: the old live CIB/bitmap enter it and the newly consumed pair leave it. Dropping explicitIpFqEntries silently retains the source queue. apfsWriter_foreignMultiChunkCowInsertRoundTrips asserts the output queue contains both old live blocks and excludes both new live blocks, so this mutant fails.
